name: lima-sandbox
description: The isolated (virtual-machine) execution-isolation tier, backed by Lima (Linux virtual machines on macOS and Linux). Runs an agent-influenced command inside a Lima instance through `limactl shell` instead of on the host, so the virtual machine — not a host path filter — is the boundary. Registers as a `sandbox` provider through the SandboxProvider seam: a cached availability probe greys the tier out with a reason when the instance is stopped, and host paths are translated to their in-guest mount location so a run opened "inside the sandbox" resolves the same working directory.
author: PersonalClaw

x-meta.label: Lima instance name
x-meta.help: The limactl instance a run executes inside (limactl start <name>). Both the availability probe and every launch target this instance.

x-meta.label: vCPUs
x-meta.help: Advisory record of the instance's CPU allocation, surfaced in the degradation dialog. Lima itself owns the running instance's real limits.

x-meta.label: Memory
x-meta.help: Advisory record of the instance's memory allocation (e.g. 4GiB).

x-meta.label: Disk
x-meta.help: Advisory record of the instance's disk allocation (e.g. 20GiB).

x-meta.label: Lima template
x-meta.help: The Lima template the instance was created from (default, ubuntu, fedora, ...). Recorded for the degradation dialog; creating the instance stays a user step.

x-meta.label: Availability probe TTL (seconds)
x-meta.help: How long a probe of the instance's Running/Stopped state is cached. Stopping the instance greys the tier out within one TTL.
